title: Bishops VS Rook
reviewNotes: Four branches, 21 exact positions from the complete six-piece source board. Stable diagrams resolve captioned first Bd6 as Be6 from a2, followed by Bd6 from a3. Compared rook fork, rook pin, actual stalemate after Bxb3 and drawn Bg8 route. ...Kb1 Bxf6 fork completion is independently labeled.
transcript: Fools will resign. Wise players will accept a draw, but only a true genius would be able to win from this position. The last square bishop is under attack, but there are not many squares that we can move this bishop to. Going for example to D5 would lose the bishop to this rook check that forces the king to move and then there would be a pin. But other moves like for example bishop to G8 would allow the brilliant counter shot from black. Rook to B3 an incredible sacrifice that of course cannot be accepted because if the bishop was to take this rook, this would actually be a stalemate and a draw. But there's also another issue. This move is a fork and it seems like white can set up a little trap with a move like bishop to D6 because now if you take the pawn, this is actually a checkmate in one move. But unfortunately this doesn't work. Black doesn't have to take the pawn. He can give a check with the rook and after the king moves, now it is safe to take the pawn and so this will be a draw. So if we go back to the starting position, it seems like white has no way of making any progress. But white has foreseen a very interesting idea starting with bishop to D6. This seems to allow rook to B3. This is the fork and sacrifice that we just looked at. The rook cannot be taken. But white carelessly continues with bishop to D6. Another seemingly useless move. The rook just gives a check and then collects the pawn. We just looked at this position. The rook is going to be enough to hold off the two bishops and this is just a draw, right? Well, not exactly. We didn't look at this exact position and actually incredibly white is completely winning after the brilliant and majestic king to E2. Some of you might think, well, this doesn't make any sense. Yes, we are attacking the rook, but the rook has so many squares that it can go to. Surely there is going to be a safe one. But as it turns out, these bishops are creating an incredible barricade that covers pretty much every single square that the rook can go to. The king is covering all four of these squares, which allows only two options for this rook. Either the C3 square or the F6 square. But some of you might have noticed that these squares are both on the same line as the king. Meaning that if the rook goes to F6, there's going to be a fork, picking up the rook and winning the game. And if the rook goes to C3, there's going to be a pin. And we're going to again pick up this rook and white will win the game.
